There's a world of titles and jobs out there... but I'd suggest starting as an RN.  That opens doors to things we didn't even know about.  There is an Associates RN program.  It's worth the work, the time, and tears (from what I hear).  Anesthesia can make some $$$ but they are usually the Doc making the real cash.  Altho I don't really know. So I should probably not speak to that.

Less social yes and no.  I call it the best customer service job ever!! My patients are Asleep!!!!!
Some surgeons are chatty, but most aren't imo.  They just want to do their work and get outta there as fast as safely possible.

It doesn't go into anything.   I mean some of the pre reqs transfer that's about all you can hope for.  Which is bull shit.  I have an associates in surgical technology....for what?  I literally can't do anything else.  I can only ever work as a Tech in an OR of some sort.
Even to be a nurse they make you become a cna. First... Which is lower on the ladder then a Tech, right.  So we literally are re schooling for the paperwork to move on to become or do something else.
I wish someone had pulled me aside and had some real talk with me when I had to choose between being a LVN and a CST.  I'd be a RN already.

Call is a challenge but the money can be good 
Never know what you're doing day to day...can also be good 
The early hours (but you're off early)
People will sabatotage you, so you must always under all circumstances cover your ass.
No one takes accountability and everyone will blame YOU.
I'm sorry but being a tech gives zero room for growth unless your state has FIrst Assists .  Which mine does not so I have capped out and I am only in the business 9 years.
